scenes.heading: What is Newton's second law?
scenes.subtitle: Force, mass and acceleration
scenes.narration: Newton's second law tells us how a force changes the motion of an object.

scenes.heading: The law in one line
scenes.narration: The law says that force equals mass times acceleration.

steps.narration: F stands for the net force on the object, measured in newtons.
m stands for mass, measured in kilograms.
The last symbol stands for acceleration, which tells us how fast the velocity changes.
A cart has a mass of two kilograms.
You push it with a net force of ten newtons.
So the acceleration is ten divided by two, which is five metres per second squared.
For the same mass, a bigger force gives a bigger acceleration.
For the same force, a heavier object speeds up more slowly.
In short, force equals mass times acceleration.
